title: How many zeros does a thousand lakh have?
description: A lakh, a crore and an arab are each built as a hundred times the name before, and the zeros are counted at every step. The same counting is used on a thousand lakh and on a hundred thousand. Keeko then raises a hand, thinking a thousand lakh makes a crore.
teaching_notes: One idea: multiplying by a hundred adds two zeros and multiplying by a thousand adds three, so the zeros of the parts add up. Ask the class how many zeros a thousand has before any lakh is built. Watch for students who think a thousand lakh is a crore because a crore is the next name.

source: Show that a lakh is a hundred thousands, a crore a hundred lakhs and an arab a hundred crores. Then find the zeros in a thousand lakh and in a hundred thousand
video_script.why: The child can place commas in both systems and now sees how lakh, crore and arab are built by hundreds, and what that does to the zeros.
video_script.substitution: A lakh is a hundred times a thousand, a crore a hundred times a lakh and an arab a hundred times a crore; the zeros of the parts add.
video_script.anchor: The chain of names thousand, lakh, crore and arab, each drawn as one with its zeros.
video_script.wrong_answer: a thousand lakh makes a crore
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks a thousand lakh makes a crore. A crore is only a hundred lakh, so a thousand lakh is ten times a crore, with one more zero.
video_script.payoff_line: A thousand lakh has eight zeros, and a hundred thousand has five zeros
never_show: the zeros of a thousand lakh before step two
maths_rules: a thousand lakh: 1000 × 1,00,000 = 10,00,00,000, zeros 3 + 5 = 8, and it is ten crore
a hundred thousand: 100 × 1000 = 1,00,000, zeros 2 + 3 = 5, and it is one lakh
the slip: a thousand lakh is not a crore; a crore is 100 lakh and a thousand lakh is 10 crore
video_script.design: One idea: each name is a hundred times the one before, and zeros add when numbers are multiplied. Wrong idea: Keeko says a thousand lakh makes a crore. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, take one thousand and multiply by one hundred. That gives one lakh, which has five zeros.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>One hundred times one lakh gives one crore, which has seven zeros.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>One hundred times one crore gives one arab, which has nine zeros. Each time, two more zeros come.

marks.m3: 10,00,00,000 is written and its zeros are circled

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, a thousand lakh is one thousand times one lakh.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A thousand has three zeros and a lakh has five, so the zeros come to eight.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The number is ten crore.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: hundred thousand = 100 × 1000 = 1,00,000; zeros 2 + 3 = 5, the same as one lakh

marks.m3: 1,00,000 is written and matched with one lakh

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, a hundred thousand is one hundred times one thousand.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A hundred has two zeros and a thousand has three, so the zeros come to five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>This is the same as one lakh, as step one showed.

marks.m1: the answer line is written and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>A thousand lakh has eight zeros, and a hundred thousand has five zeros.
